# Swift and Apple-platform secure coding

- Validate external and decoded data into explicit models. Do not force-unwrap, force-cast, or index attacker-controlled values; return controlled errors instead of crashes.
- Store credentials and long-lived tokens in Keychain with the narrowest accessibility and access-control settings. Do not place secrets in source, `UserDefaults`, plists, logs, backups, or pasteboards.
- Use `SecRandomCopyBytes`/CryptoKit for security values and standard authenticated encryption/signature APIs. Do not implement cryptography or disable trust evaluation.
- Keep App Transport Security enabled. If an exception is required, scope it to the exact domain and capability; never install an accept-all certificate challenge handler.
- Validate deep links/universal links by scheme, host, path, state, and authenticated context. Do not execute privileged actions solely from link parameters.
- Constrain WebView navigation/content, disable unnecessary JavaScript/file access, use exact message-handler schemas, and never render untrusted HTML in a privileged origin.
- Use prepared/bound database operations and safe file URLs. Resolve paths within the app container and apply data-protection classes appropriate to sensitivity.
- Protect local authentication fallback and Keychain access with correct `LAContext` policy. A successful biometric prompt is not authorization for a server resource.
- Minimize exported URL schemes, entitlements, background modes, inter-app sharing, and sensitive notification content. Redact screen/app-switcher content when required by the threat model.
- Bound network response size/time, parsing, image/document work, concurrency, and retries. Cancel obsolete work and make retried state changes idempotent.
- Avoid sensitive crash/log data and ensure production builds do not expose debug menus, test endpoints, or verbose network logging.
